title: Addition is lambda definable

statement_spans.label: author prop environment with its own label prop:add-ld (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 459-462

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the prop: Two encodings: Add = lambda a b. lambda f x. a f (b f x) iterates f n and then m times, reducing to the numeral n+m; Add' = lambda a b. a Succ b applies the lambda-defined successor n times to the numeral m, also reducing to n+m. (source lines 464-490)

standard_prerequisites.name: Successor lambda-definability (lambda-definability unit, Proposition prop:succ-ld, source line 415)
standard_prerequisites.use: The second encoding Add' = lambda a b. a Succ b needs Succ to lambda-define the successor function.

standard_prerequisites.name: Church numeral encoding (lambda-definability unit, earlier section: the numeral for n is the term lambda f x. f^n x)
standard_prerequisites.use: The numeral for n applied to f and x reduces to f^n x, which drives both reduction chains.

core_obligations: Verify the first encoding (proof lines 465-478): Add = lambda a b. lambda f x. a f (b f x); applied to the numerals n and m it reduces through n f (m f x) = f^n (f^m x) to the numeral for n+m.

Verify the second encoding (proof lines 479-489): Add' = lambda a b. a Succ b reduces to the numeral n applied to Succ and m, i.e. Succ iterated n times at m, which is the numeral for n+m since Succ lambda-defines the successor.
proof_roadmap: Reduce Add applied to numerals n and m along the iterated-f chain (proof lines 465-478).
Reduce Add' applied to numerals n and m through iterated Succ (proof lines 479-489).
difficulty_reason: Two explicit terms, each with a written reduction chain; the second leans on the named successor proposition, 27-line proof, no omissions.
